tasks.title: Lecture #21
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk on a podcast about psychology.
tasks.transcript:
Podcast Host: Did you see that new thriller movie that came out last week? I did and loved it. The action, the plot twists… I was totally captivated. Time just flew by. Not a single thought occurred to me that was unrelated to the movie. What I experienced is what psychologists call hard fascination. Hard fascination means intense focus and concentration. Whether it’s TV programs, video games… hard fascination is all too easy to come by in this modern world.
There’s another type of fascination- soft fascination. There’s still effortless attention, meaning that no special effort is required for you to stay focused, but there’s still room for other thoughts. When I take a walk in the park and look at the flowers and trees, for example, I might be thinking in the back of my mind about my dinner plans.
Now, one thing to know is hard fascination causes mental fatigue. The mind is so intensely focused that it gets tired fast. What follows mental fatigue? You might find yourself easily distracted, irritable, and stressed. Soft fascination, in contrast, engages a different part of the brain- - the DMN, or Default Mode Network, which soothes the mind and helps combat mental fatigue. So next time you feel like your mind is on overload, turn off the TV, put down your phone. Take a walk, or simply sit and stare at the clouds.

questions.stem: What is the topic of the talk?

options.B: How to keep the mind focused

questions.analysis: 答案：C 题目问的是：这段讲话的主题是什么？ 定位原文： What I experienced is what psychologists call hard fascination. Hard fascination means intense focus and concentration. ... There’s another type of fascination—soft fascination. There’s still effortless attention, meaning that no special effort is required for you to stay focused, but there’s still room for other thoughts. 选项分析： A. How psychologists study attention（心理学家如何研究注意力）。讲话介绍了两种 fascination 的概念，但并未讨论研究方法，所以A选项错误。 B. How to keep the mind focused（如何保持注意力集中）。讲话虽在结尾给出建议，但主要内容是对两种 fascination 的区分和介绍，所以B选项错误。 C. Two types of fascination（两种 fascination 类型）。讲话围绕 hard fascination 和 soft fascination 展开，分别解释其定义、特点及影响，因此C选项正确。 D. The benefits of hard fascination（硬 fascination 的好处）。讲话指出 hard fascination 会导致精神疲劳，并未强调其好处，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention a movie?

options.A: To compare different types of movies
options.B: To introduce a concept in psychology
options.C: To explain how movies affect emotions
options.D: To encourage listeners to watch more movies

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：演讲者为什么提到电影？ 定位原文： Did you see that new thriller movie that came out last week? I did and loved it. The action, the plot twists… I was totally captivated. Time just flew by. Not a single thought occurred to me that was unrelated to the movie. What I experienced is what psychologists call hard fascination. 选项分析： A. To compare different types of movies（为了比较不同类型的电影）。讲话只提到一部电影，并未进行类型比较，所以A选项错误。 B. To introduce a concept in psychology（为了引入一个心理学概念）。讲话通过描述自己观看电影的体验，引出 hard fascination 这一心理学概念，因此B选项正确。 C. To explain how movies affect emotions（为了解释电影如何影响情绪）。讲话未深入探讨情绪影响，所以C选项错误。 D. To encourage listeners to watch more movies（为了鼓励听众多看电影）。讲话未表达鼓励观影的意图，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about her walk in the park?

options.A: It is similar to her experience watching a good movie.
options.B: Her mind has space for thoughts unrelated to nature.
options.C: She needs to put in special effort to stay focused on flowers and trees.
options.D: She gets mental fatigue from her mind engaging in hard fascination.

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：演讲者对她自己在公园散步有什么说法？ 定位原文： When I take a walk in the park and look at the flowers and trees, for example, I might be thinking in the back of my mind about my dinner plans. 选项分析： A. It is similar to her experience watching a good movie（这和她观看好电影的经历相似）。观看电影是 hard fascination，公园散步是 soft fascination，两者不同，所以A选项错误。 B. Her mind has space for thoughts unrelated to nature（她的思维有空间容纳与自然无关的想法）。讲话明确指出散步时她会在脑海深处思考晚餐计划，因此B选项正确。 C. She needs to put in special effort to stay focused on flowers and trees（她需要付出特别的努力才能专注于花草树木）。讲话指出 soft fascination 是 effortless attention（无需努力即可保持专注），所以C选项错误。 D. She gets mental fatigue from her mind engaging in hard fascination（她因大脑处于 hard fascination 状态而感到精神疲劳）。公园散步属于 soft fascination，不会导致精神疲劳，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about Default Mode Network?

options.A: It is involved in soft fascination.
options.B: It leads to irritability and stress.
options.C: It is easily tired from overuse.
options.D: Its effect is unknown to psychologists.

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目问的是：演讲者对默认模式网络有什么说法？ 定位原文： Soft fascination, in contrast, engages a different part of the brain—the DMN, or Default Mode Network, which soothes the mind and helps combat mental fatigue. 选项分析： A. It is involved in soft fascination（它与 soft fascination 相关）。讲话明确指出 soft fascination 会激活默认模式网络，因此A选项正确。 B. It leads to irritability and stress（它导致烦躁和压力）。讲话指出导致烦躁和压力的是 hard fascination 带来的精神疲劳，而非 DMN，所以B选项错误。 C. It is easily tired from overuse（它因过度使用而容易疲劳）。讲话未提及 DMN 会疲劳，所以C选项错误。 D. Its effect is unknown to psychologists（其效果对心理学家来说是未知的）。讲话明确描述了 DMN 的作用，说明其效果已知，所以D选项错误。
